content: Erythromycin is an antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication belongs to the macrolide class of antibiotics and works by stopping the growth of bacteria. It may also be prescribed to prevent certain bacterial infections. How to Use: Take erythromycin orally as directed by your doctor, typically before a meal. For optimal absorption, it is best taken on an empty stomach. Do not crush or chew the medication, as it has a bitter taste. Swallow it whole. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. To achieve the best results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If you are using this medication to treat an infection, continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may allow the infection to return. If you are taking this medication to prevent bacterial infections, follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain or cramping, and loss of appetite. Taking the medication with food may help reduce these symptoms. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, erythromycin may cause a severe intestinal condition called Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea. This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Precautions: Before taking erythromycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other macrolide antibiotics (e.g., azithromycin, clarithromycin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Erythromycin may cause a condition affecting the heart rhythm (QT prolongation), which can lead to serious (rarely fatal) irregular heartbeat. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions (e.g., low potassium or magnesium levels) or are taking other drugs that may cause QT prolongation. Severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting can also increase the risk of QT prolongation. Erythromycin may interfere with live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine), reducing their effectiveness. Some erythromycin products may contain sodium, which should be considered if you are on a sodium-restricted diet. This medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can affect the removal of erythromycin from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Erythromycin can also slow the removal of other drugs from your body, which may affect how they work. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., urine tests), possibly causing false results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store erythromycin at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
